To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

SMR is a simple yet very powerful technique for implementing fault-tolerant systems, that SMR is the only technique that is both theoretically and practically proven to work, that SMR can be implemented using simple and efficient protocols, and that there is a large number of practical applications for SMR.

(a) SMR protocols are a good choice when the application needs to tolerate Byzantine failures and the application can be described as a set of state machines, (b) SMR protocols provide high availability and consistency but they have a high performance overhead, and (c) SMR protocols can be improved to reduce the performance overhead, to improve modularity and to increase their resilience to attacks.
SMR can be implemented in a modular and efficient way, and can be applied in several contexts.

the following questions: What are the fundamentals of SMR? How can we implement SMR protocols? What applications can we use for implementing SMR?

we have been working on the theory and practice of SMR for more than 20 years.

the SMR paradigm is a mature and robust approach for building dependable services, with many successful applications, including the core services of some well-known cloud computing platforms.

, despite its simplicity, SMR is a very powerful technique that has been successfully applied to a number of different scenarios.
